profile.summary: Borzoi is a neural network that predicts RNA-seq coverage, the read depth along genes in different cell types and tissues, directly from DNA sequence. It takes a 524 kb stretch of human or mouse genome and outputs predicted coverage for thousands of experiments in 32 bp bins. Comparing predictions for the reference and the variant sequence gives scores for a variant's effect on gene expression, splicing and polyadenylation.

summary_quotes.text: Here, we introduce Borzoi, a model that learns to predict cell-type-specific and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence.
convolutional neural networks trained to predict RNA-seq coverage at 32bp resolution given 524kb input sequences
we isolate and accurately score DNA variant effects across multiple layers of regulation, including transcription, splicing and polyadenylation.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Borzoi is a supervised model, not a language model: it is trained to reproduce measured coverage tracks. It uses the core Enformer architecture, a tower of convolution and pooling blocks followed by self-attention blocks at 128 bp resolution, then a U-net that upsamples back to 32 bp resolution. The training targets are RNA-seq coverage from ENCODE and GTEx plus the Enformer training data (CAGE, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq). Variant effects are computed from the difference between predicted coverage for the reference and the alternate sequence, summarised by statistics such as logSED for gene expression, COVR for polyadenylation and nDi for splicing.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The published model is four replicates trained with identical data splits, each distributed as a human and a mouse .h5 weight file. The authors report that an ensemble of the four replicates generally performed better than any single replicate. A separate collection of smaller Mini Borzoi models, trained on subsets of data types or with architecture changes, is also published. The repository has legacy and latest data transforms; the legacy transforms match the manuscript. A result should say which replicates were used, whether they were averaged, and which transform was applied.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised sequence-to-coverage model (convolutional network with self-attention)

quotes.text: Borzoi models, which are convolutional neural networks trained to predict RNA-seq coverage

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Enformer core (convolution and subsampling tower, then self-attention blocks with relative positional encodings at 128 bp resolution) followed by U-net upsampling with skip connections to 32 bp resolution.

quotes.text: followed by a stack of self-attention layers with relative positional encodings operating at 128 bp resolution, similar to the Enformer architecture. The output is then repeatedly upsampled and put through additional convolution layers with matched U-net connections to predict at 32 bp resolution.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A 524 kb DNA sequence (human hg38 or mouse mm10). Variant scoring scripts take SNVs in a VCF file, a targets file and a parameters file.

facts.value: Predicted coverage tracks in 32 bp bins for RNA-seq, CAGE, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq experiments; the variant scripts write scores (logSED, logD2, COVR, nDi) to HDF5 files.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not reported for the full-size published model in the sources read. The ablation models were reduced to about 30 million trainable parameters.

quotes.text: Therefore, we reduced their size (393,192 bp input length, ~30 million trainable parameters, four self-attention heads per layer)

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Uniformly processed RNA-seq from ENCODE (866 human and 279 mouse datasets), two to three replicates per GTEx tissue processed by recount3, and the Enformer training data (CAGE, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq), tiled in 524 kb windows across the human and mouse genomes. The processed data are in a requester-pays Google Cloud bucket of several TB.

quotes.text: We chose to work with uniformly processed RNA-seq from ENCODE, providing 866 human and 279 mouse datasets
Training examples are extracted in tiled 524 kb windows spanning the human and mouse genome
This data bucket is large (multiple TB) and thus set to "Requester Pays".

strengths.text: Scores a variant's effect on several layers of gene regulation from one model: expression, splicing and polyadenylation.

quotes.text: Borzoi enables variant scoring and interpretation through multiple layers of regulation, including transcription, splicing and polyadenylation

strengths.text: Predictions are specific to cell type and tissue, because each output track corresponds to a training experiment.

quotes.text: a model that learns to predict cell-type-specific and tissue-specific RNA-seq coverage from DNA sequence

strengths.text: Long input window: 524 kb, enough to cover the exons and many regulatory elements of long mammalian genes.

quotes.text: the long span of mammalian genes means that we must also work with very long sequences to cover all exons and relevant regulatory elements

strengths.text: Training data, QTL benchmark sets and paper replication scripts are published alongside the weights.

run_guide.summary: Install baskerville-tf and borzoi, download the four published replicates and the hg38 genome, and score a small set of SNVs for gene expression effects with the legacy tutorial script.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 and TensorFlow 2.15.x, installed in a conda environment.
Network access to storage.googleapis.com and hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu; download_models.sh uses wget and fetches the hg38 genome FASTA.
GPU and memory needs for inference are not stated in the sources read.
Code is Apache-2.0; no licence is stated for the weights.

steps.shell:
export BORZOI_DIR=/home/<user_path>/borzoi

steps.title: Score SNVs for gene expression effects
steps.explanation: The legacy tutorial uses the pre-trained published model. The path assumes borzoi was cloned into the home directory, as the tutorial does. The script runs borzoi_sed.py with replicate f3c0 on the tutorial's snps_expr.vcf and writes to snp_sed/f3c0. Other scripts in the same folder score gene-agnostic expression, polyadenylation and splicing.

quotes.text: cd ~/borzoi/tutorials/legacy/score_variants ./score_expr_sed.sh
This example uses the pre-trained, published Borzoi model to predict variant effects.

borzoi_sed.py -o snp_sed/f3c0 --rc --stats logSED,logD2 -u -t ../../../examples/targets_gtex.txt ../../../examples/params_pred.json ../../../examples/saved_models/f3c0/train/model0_best.h5 snps_expr.vcf

outputs: Variant prediction HDF5 output in snp_sed/f3c0 holding two statistics: logSED (gene expression log fold change) and logD2 (bin-level L2 norm across the coverage of the gene's exons).
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The tutorial scores the SNVs in its own example VCF with one replicate; scoring other variants or averaging replicates needs the script arguments, which were not read here.
The weight files are not versioned, so the downloaded files cannot be checked against a published checksum.

notes: The existing source (Manzo et al. 2025) is a benchmark that evaluated Borzoi. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so store_bytes is false for it. Only the calico repositories, which the paper names as the official code, were used. The run guide pins baskerville-tf to its head commit on 2026-11-26 without having read that commit.
